title: Completion-unit-normalized scalar comparison for pullback
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite normed field extension, put $A=\mathcal O_E$ and fix a uniformizer $\varpi$. Let $k$ have positive prime characteristic different from $\ell$, and let all schemes mentioned be separated and of finite type over $k$. Require explicitly that each scheme is Noetherian and finite dimensional and that $\ell$ is invertible in its local rings. On the small pro-etale site put $A_T=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_T$ and $E_T(V)=C(|V|,E)$, with pointwise operations; regard $E_T$ as an $A_T$-algebra through the canonical isomorphism $A_T\cong(V\mapsto C(|V|,A))$ of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction] followed by postcomposition with the inclusion $A\subset E$. Use the integral category $\mathcal I_T=\Dbc(T,A)$ of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] and its raw scalar localization $\mathcal R_T=\mathcal I_T[1/\varpi]$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Write $F_T=E_T\otimes^L_{A_T}-$ as in [lem-weil-pbc-realization-scalar-functor]. For any $k$-morphism $h:T\to U$ and $K\in\mathcal I_U$, the actual coefficient structure map $c_h:h^{-1}A_U\to A_T$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] is the canonical isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] for the tower $(A/\varpi^n)_{n\geq1}$; under the identifications $A_W\cong(V\mapsto C(|V|,A))$ for $W=T,U$ it is the adjunct of precomposition of continuous functions with the projections $V\times_UT\to V$. Ordinary module pullback $P_hK=Lh_A^*K$ lies in $\mathcal I_T$. Its specified quotient-tower completion unit $\gamma_{h,K}:P_hK\to Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$ is an isomorphism. The natural comparison
$$\alpha_{h,K}:F_TLh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K\xrightarrow{F_T(\gamma_{h,K}^{-1})}F_TP_hK\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh_c^*F_UK$$
uses the actual inverse-image/localization comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-inverse-image-coherence]. Here $Lh_c^*$ is the actual continuous $E$-coefficient derived module inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], encoded in [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category], taken with the coefficient isomorphism $h^{-1}E_U\cong E_T$ obtained from $c_h$ by localization at $\varpi$, which precomposes continuous $E$-valued functions. It preserves localization units, sends pulled fractions to the pulled numerators with the same denominator, and respects identity and composition comparisons of pullback, in the following sense. For a further $k$-morphism $j:U\to V$ let $p:P_hP_j\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{jh}$ be the inverse of the ordinary comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] and $q_E:Lh_c^*Lj_c^*\xrightarrow{\sim}L(jh)_c^*$ the corresponding $E$-coefficient comparison. On integral objects the completed composition comparison $q:Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Lj^*_{\mathrm{comp}}\xrightarrow{\sim}L(jh)^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$ is the unique isomorphism with $q_K\,\gamma_{h,Lj^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K}\,P_h(\gamma_{j,K})=\gamma_{jh,K}\,p_K$, and the completed identity comparison is the ordinary identity comparison $e:P_{\mathrm{id}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ precomposed with $\gamma_{\mathrm{id}}^{-1}$. Then $\alpha_{jh,K}F_T(q_K)=q_{E}\,Lh_c^*(\alpha_{j,K})\,\alpha_{h,Lj^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K}$ and $e_E\,\alpha_{\mathrm{id},K}=F_T(e_K\gamma_{\mathrm{id},K}^{-1})$, with $e_E$ the ordinary $E$-coefficient identity comparison. These comparisons also induce those on the raw rationalized categories. No cartesian-square or properness hypothesis is needed.

source.place: 6.6.11 and Remark 6.8.15: ordinary and completed pullback scalar comparison

proof.text: Set $Q_n=A/\varpi^n$. The coefficient datum of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] supplies the extending nonarchimedean absolute value, DVR and finite residue field; hence these are finite rings by [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] to this tower. Its isomorphism $c_h:h^{-1}A_U\to A_T$ has precisely the finite-projection equations defining the coefficient map in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]; uniqueness of a map into a limit identifies the two actual maps. Under the continuous-function identification in [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction], precomposition with $V\times_U T\to V$ has those same projections: reducing the value of a continuous function modulo $\varpi^n$ commutes with precomposition. It therefore gives this same $c_h$. Its compatibility with coefficient inclusion and composition is [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-pullback-composition]; profinite comparison also supplies identity and composition. In particular it carries the pulled uniformizer to the chosen uniformizer, without any assertion that inverse image preserves arbitrary inverse limits.

source.place: Definitions 6.5.1 and 6.8.1; finite-projection normalization of the coefficient pullback

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] with the isomorphism of step 1, ordinary $P_h=Lh_A^*$ is exact module inverse image applied termwise. Use (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] for $K$. Pull back its finite strata by forming $T\times_U U_i$, rather than merely taking set-theoretic images. Inverse images preserve disjointness, the covering union and local closedness, so these immersions form a finite stratification in [def-constructible-stratification], omitting empty strata. The local trivializing pro-etale covers pull back to covers: weakly etale maps and fpqc covering families are stable under base change by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change] and [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. On each pulled-back chart, pullback composition [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] and the tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identify the restricted object with $A_T\otimes_A^L P$, for the same bounded finite-projective $A$-complex $P$. Concretely each term is the image of the same finite idempotent matrix, and each differential is the same matrix with its entries mapped into the pulled coefficient sheaf. Thus (ii)$\Rightarrow$(i) of the characterization gives $P_hK\in\mathcal I_T$, including the compatible etale-origin witnesses and uniform reduction bounds. All hypotheses of that characterization hold on $T$ and $U$ by the statement.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, stratified perfect characterization; Remark 6.8.15, ordinary pullback

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-pullback-derived-tower] with $R_U=A_U$, $R_T=A_T$ and quotient tower $(Q_n)_U$. Step 1 identifies its pulled tower with $(Q_n)_T$, including transitions. Its isomorphism $\tau_K$ identifies the pulled reduction tower of $K$ with the reduction tower of $P_hK$ and, crucially, sends the pulled strict augmentation to the actual quotient augmentation. Apply the derived-limit functor and its constant-tower-adjunction unit as in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Naturality of that adjunction unit and the augmentation equation for $\tau_K$ identify the specified $\gamma_{h,K}$ with the canonical quotient-tower completion unit of $P_hK$; this is equality of the functorially induced maps, not an inference from equality of their projections. Step 2 makes $P_hK$ intrinsically complete. Now [lem-weil-pbc-intrinsic-to-tower-complete] says exactly that this constant-tower-adjunction unit followed by the strict quotient augmentation is invertible. Therefore the specified $\gamma_{h,K}$ is an isomorphism. Both objects lie in the full integral subcategory; the completed one does because it is isomorphic to $P_hK$, using the characterization of step 2.

source.place: Tag 099M, lemma-naive-completion; strict augmentation normalization supplied by the cited tower comparison

proof.text:
The continuous-coefficient theorem identifies $E_W$ with the sheafified localization $A_W[1/\varpi]$ for $W=T,U$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-inverse-image-coherence] to the geometric inverse image and transport its coefficients along the actual $c_h$ of step 1. Its ring comparison gives the continuous rational coefficient map: both maps precompose continuous functions, as follows first for integral numerators and then for fractions from the localization unit. Write $Q_h=Lh_c^*$. Invert the module comparison $\beta_h$ of that node to obtain the ordinary scalar comparison
$$B_{h,K}:F_TP_hK\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_hF_UK.$$
This is the comparison for the actual scalar-extension functor of [lem-weil-pbc-realization-scalar-functor], since that functor is tensor with this very localization. The cited coherence node gives exactness, unbounded derived comparison and naturality, so no bounded resolution interchange is implicit here. If $\lambda_W:M\to F_WM$ is the localization unit, its normalization reads $B_h\lambda_T=h^{-1}\lambda_U$, as maps of underlying integral-module objects, after the canonical scalar-restriction and pullback identifications. Locally $B_h$ sends $(h^{-1}m)/\varpi^n$ to $h^{-1}(m/\varpi^n)$. These are sheaf-local fraction representatives, with no claim of a single global denominator.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2 and Remark 6.8.15; localization inverse-image comparison with its unit normalization

proof.text:
Put $C_h=Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$ and define $\alpha_h=B_hF_T(\gamma_h^{-1})$. Step 3 and step 4 make this a natural isomorphism with exactly the source, target and order of factors asserted in the statement. The construction of the quotient augmentation and its adjunction unit in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] is natural, so inverses of its now invertible components are natural as well. The precise unit normalization is
$$\alpha_h F_T(\gamma_h)\lambda_{T,P_hK}=h^{-1}(\lambda_{U,K}),$$
as maps of underlying integral-module objects with the canonical scalar-restriction and pullback identifications. Indeed $F_T(\gamma_h^{-1})F_T(\gamma_h)=1$, leaving the unit equation for $B_h$ from step 4. The same cancellation proves the asserted fraction formula after identifying completed pullback with ordinary pullback by this specified unit; it does not choose a second comparison.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; agent calculation of the completion-unit normalization

proof.text:
For $h:T\to U$, $j:U\to V$ write $p:P_hP_j\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{jh}$ for the inverse of the comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. On the integral constructible categories every completion unit here is invertible by steps 2--3. The canonical completed composition comparison $q:C_hC_j\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{jh}$ is then uniquely determined by
$$q\,\gamma_{h,C_jK}\,P_h(\gamma_{j,K})=\gamma_{jh,K}\,p_K.$$
Explicitly $q_K=\gamma_{jh,K}\,p_K\,P_h(\gamma_{j,K}^{-1})\,\gamma_{h,C_jK}^{-1}$, which exists and is unique because the precomposed factors are isomorphisms. This is the completed composition comparison of the statement, which is defined by this normalization; [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] specifies no other composition comparison, and its completion units are the quotient-augmentation maps identified in step 3 through [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-pullback-derived-tower]. Naturality of $q$ in $K$ follows from naturality of $\gamma$, $p$ and $P_h$. For the identity the same argument gives the inverse of its completion unit followed by the ordinary identity comparison. This argument compares actual augmentation-induced maps; it does not use joint faithfulness of projections from a derived limit.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; agent normalization calculation for the constructible restriction

proof.text:
Let $q_E:Q_hQ_j\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{jh}$ be ordinary rational pullback composition. The identity and composition assertions of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-inverse-image-coherence] give
$$B_{jh}F_T(p)=q_E\,Q_h(B_j)\,B_{h,P_j}.$$
To check the required completed equation
$$\alpha_{jh}F_T(q)=q_E\,Q_h(\alpha_j)\,\alpha_{h,C_j},$$
precompose both sides with the invertible $F_T(\gamma_{h,C_j}P_h\gamma_j)$. Step 6 changes the left side into $B_{jh}F_T(p)$. On the right first cancel $F_T\gamma_h^{-1}F_T\gamma_h$; naturality of $B_h$ at $\gamma_j$ moves $F_T(P_h\gamma_j)$ past $B_h$, where it cancels the factor $Q_hF_U\gamma_j^{-1}$. The result is $q_EQ_h(B_j)B_{h,P_j}$, equal to the left side by the displayed ordinary equation. Cancel the precomposition. For identity the identical cancellation leaves the identity equation for $B$. Thus the specified comparisons respect both identity and composition, with the actual completion units retained.

Ordinary pullback is exact and $A$-linear by the termwise description, and completed pullback on the integral subcategories is naturally isomorphic to it by $\gamma$. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] to extend these functors and their natural comparisons to the raw rationalizations of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. On a fraction $u/\varpi^n$ the extension is $P_h(u)/\varpi^n$ (or $C_h(u)/\varpi^n$), while [lem-weil-pbc-realization-scalar-functor] sends it to $\varpi^{-n}F(u)$. Since every comparison is $A$-linear and the same uniformizer is pulled back, its naturality equation for $u/\varpi^n$ is the integral equation for $u$ multiplied by $\varpi^{-n}$. This proves naturality and the identical-denominator formula after rationalization. The inverse, unit, identity and composition equations persist under the localization functor, by functoriality and the unique extension of natural transformations in the transport node. Objects are unchanged, so no Karoubi envelope or new lattice choice enters.
